subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram DMs can still land in agent:main:main, polluting heartbeat/main session after #40519

question: Should maintainers split the remaining work into a heartbeat wake precedence bugfix first, or also change Telegram DMs away from the documented default main-session behavior?
rationale: The heartbeat precedence path is source-reproducible as a bug, but changing Telegram default DM routing would alter documented cross-channel `session.dmScope` compatibility and was already rejected as an implicit product-policy shift in #41939.

options.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
options.body: Rework or sponsor a current-main fix so explicit `heartbeat.session` wins for event-triggered wakes, while leaving Telegram DM defaults governed by `session.dmScope`.

options.title: Bundle safer DM defaults
options.body: Change or document Telegram or cross-channel DM isolation defaults in the same effort, accepting the compatibility and migration implications for existing main-session users.

options.title: Defer to per-session heartbeat design
options.body: Fold this into the broader native per-session heartbeat scheduling work, which may be cleaner long term but leaves the forced-session contamination path unresolved longer.

recommendation.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
recommendation.body: Rework or sponsor a current-main fix so explicit `heartbeat.session` wins for event-triggered wakes, while leaving Telegram DM defaults governed by `session.dmScope`.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans heartbeat runtime behavior, session routing compatibility, and prior mainline merges in the implicated area.
